svg.title: Idempotent Consumer
svg.desc: Idempotent Consumer. Remember processed message IDs so a redelivered message has no extra effect. Step 1, Why duplicates arrive: At-least-once: the ack for m-7f3 is lost, the broker delivers it again, and $40 is charged twice. Step 2, Save the ID with the work: One transaction inserts the message ID and applies the charge: both commit, or neither does. Step 3, Redelivery changes nothing: m-7f3 arrives again: the insert hits the unique key, so the handler skips the work and just acks. Step 4, Beyond your own database: The provider gets the message ID as an idempotency key, so a repeated call returns the first result.

g.text: 2 · Save the ID with the work
2 · Save the ID with the work
At-least-once: the ack for m-7f3 is lost, the broker delivers it again, and $40 is charged twice.
One transaction inserts the message ID and applies the charge: both commit, or neither does.
m-7f3 arrives again: the insert hits the unique key, so the handler skips the work and just acks.
The provider gets the message ID as an idempotency key, so a repeated call returns the first result.
The broker removes a message only when it gets the ack.
No ack in time (a crash, a timeout) and it delivers the message again.
It would rather repeat a message than lose one,
so every consumer has to expect duplicates.
the handler crashed before it could commit
the handler committed, but its ack was lost
Both look the same from the broker's side,
so it has to deliver the message again.
WHY THE ID AND THE CHARGE SHARE ONE TRANSACTION
a crash in between: the redelivery is skipped, and the charge never happens
a crash in between: the redelivery finds no ID and charges a second time
a crash leaves both saved or neither, so a redelivery is always handled correctly
The acknowledgement is not part of the transaction: it can still be lost after the commit.
A RACE IS SETTLED THE SAME WAY
A slow consumer still holds m-7f3 when the broker times out and hands it to a second one.
✓ first: it applies the charge and commits
waits for A's commit, then ✕ duplicate key: it skips the work and acknowledges
The unique key is the arbiter: exactly one insert wins.
A rollback undoes the ID and the payment row.
It cannot undo the provider's charge.
So the call can happen twice, and must be
safe to repeat: same key, same result.
key seen before: returns the stored result
